verses.verse:
शब्द कल्प मुपेक्ष्यापि वादयेत्स्वरमालिकाम्।
तानालापसमावेशम् बुद्ध्या कूर्याद् विचक्षणः।१४०।
verses.text: Even setting aside the framing of words, one may play a svaramālikā (garland of notes); the discerning player should, with intelligence, bring in tānas and ālāpas.

commentary.text: The meaning is just this: a svaramālikā (garland of notes) is made even without words, on the basis of the mātrās of the tāla. Just as, on the basis of measure (weight), a sweet can be made even without grain, from milk and sugar alone, but with the addition of grain still finer sweets can be made, in the same way, if words are added, tāla and rāga are bound together easily. But at the time of playing, the words support the player indirectly.

When, by the rules above, a bandiś (composition) of some rāga has been made in some tāla, then to perform it one should bring into it various kinds of tānas in laya (tempo) and ālāpas bound in tāla, and play with absorption.
